info.title: Apache APISIX Admin API
info.description:
The **Apache APISIX Admin API** is a RESTful interface for managing all APISIX gateway resources — routes, upstreams, services, consumers, SSL certificates, plugins, and more.

APISIX Admin API allows you to dynamically configure the API gateway without restarts. Accepted changes propagate to workers asynchronously.

Unless API key authentication is explicitly disabled with `deployment.admin.admin_key_required: false`, endpoints require an **API key**. Pass a key configured under `deployment.admin.admin_key` in APISIX's `config.yaml` using the `X-API-KEY` request header.

By default, the Admin API binds to `0.0.0.0:9180` and allows clients from `127.0.0.0/24`. The examples use `http://127.0.0.1:9180`; configure the listener and client allowlist in `config.yaml` under `deployment.admin.admin_listen` and `deployment.admin.allow_admin`.

To learn how to configure and operate APISIX, see [Get Started](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/getting-started/README/).

tags.name: Routes
tags.description:
A **Route** defines how client requests are matched and forwarded to upstream services. Routes are the most fundamental resource in APISIX — every incoming request is evaluated against configured routes.

A route must include at least one URI pattern through `uri` or `uris`, and one of: an inline `upstream`, an `upstream_id`, a `service_id`, `plugins`, or `script`.

**Key Features**
- Match by URI, host, HTTP method, headers, query parameters, and custom expressions
- Attach plugins for authentication, rate limiting, transformation, and more
- Support WebSocket proxying and gRPC transcoding
- Priority-based routing when multiple routes match

To learn how to configure routes, see [Routes](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/route/).

tags.name: Upstreams
tags.description:
An **Upstream** is a virtual host abstraction over a pool of backend service nodes. It defines how APISIX distributes traffic to your backend servers.

**Load Balancing Algorithms**
- `roundrobin` — Weighted round-robin (default)
- `chash` — Consistent hashing for session affinity
- `ewma` — Latency-based selection (exponentially weighted moving average)
- `least_conn` — Fewest active connections

**Health Checks**
Upstreams support **active** and **passive** health checks to automatically remove unhealthy nodes from the load balancing pool.

To learn how to configure upstreams, see [Upstreams](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/upstream/).

tags.name: Services
tags.description:
A **Service** is a reusable abstraction that groups an upstream and a set of plugins. Multiple routes can reference the same service, reducing configuration duplication.

When a route references a service via `service_id`, the service's upstream and plugins are merged with the route's own configuration. Route-level settings take precedence.

To learn how to configure services, see [Services](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/service/).

tags.name: Consumers
tags.description:
A **Consumer** represents an API user, application, or host that consumes your APIs. Consumers are typically used with authentication plugins (e.g., `key-auth`, `jwt-auth`) to identify callers and apply per-consumer rate limits or access controls.

Each consumer is uniquely identified by a `username` and can belong to a consumer group.

To learn how to configure consumers, see [Consumers](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/consumer/).

tags.name: Consumer Groups
tags.description:
A **Consumer Group** allows you to define shared plugin configurations that apply to multiple consumers. Instead of duplicating plugin settings across consumers, assign them to a group.

Consumers reference a group via the `group_id` field. Group-level plugins are merged with consumer-level plugins, with consumer-level taking precedence.

To learn how to configure consumer groups, see [Consumer Groups](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/consumer-group/).

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description:
A **Credential** stores authentication configuration associated with a consumer. Each credential can hold at most one authentication plugin (for example, `key-auth`, `basic-auth`, or `jwt-auth`).

Credentials are sub-resources of consumers. A consumer can have multiple credentials for the same authentication plugin when their identifying values differ, or for different authentication plugins.

To learn how to configure consumer credentials, see [Credentials](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/credential/).

tags.name: Plugins
tags.description:
**Plugins** extend APISIX's core functionality with middleware capabilities such as authentication, traffic control, observability, and request/response transformation.

Use these endpoints to query available plugins and their JSON schemas, or to hot-reload plugins without restarting APISIX.

Plugin configurations can be attached to routes, services, consumers, consumer groups, plugin configs, global rules, and stream routes through the `plugins` object. Credentials can hold at most one authentication plugin configuration.

See [Plugin Hub](https://apisix.apache.org/plugins/) for the full list of available plugins.

tags.name: Plugin Configs
tags.description:
A **Plugin Config** is a reusable set of plugin configurations that can be shared across multiple routes. Instead of duplicating plugin settings in each route, create a plugin config and reference it via `plugin_config_id`.

Route-level plugins are merged with plugin config plugins, with route-level taking precedence.

To learn how to configure reusable plugin configurations, see [Plugin Configs](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/plugin-config/).

tags.name: Plugin Metadata
tags.description:
**Plugin Metadata** configures shared settings for instances of a specific plugin across the APISIX cluster. A plugin can allow an individual instance to override a metadata setting. This is useful for plugins that need global configuration, such as log format templates.

For example, metadata for `http-logger` supplies a shared `log_format`; an instance-level `log_format` takes precedence.

To learn how to configure plugin metadata, see [Plugin Metadata](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/plugin-metadata/).

tags.name: Global Rules
tags.description:
A Global Rule applies plugins to incoming requests independently of route and service configuration. For HTTP requests, global and local plugins are interleaved by phase: global `rewrite`, local `rewrite`, global `access`, then local `access`. Plugin priority applies within each phase and scope.

To learn how to configure global rules, see [Plugin Global Rules](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/global-rule/).

tags.name: Stream Routes
tags.description:
A **Stream Route** defines TCP/UDP layer (L4) proxying rules. Unlike HTTP routes, stream routes operate at the transport layer and can proxy raw TCP and UDP connections.

Stream routes match traffic by `remote_addr`, `server_addr`, `server_port`, or the `sni` and `snis` fields for TLS connections.

**Note:** Stream mode must be enabled in `config.yaml` (`apisix.proxy_mode: stream` or `http&stream`) before creating stream routes.

To learn how to configure stream routes, see [Stream Routes](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/stream-proxy/).

tags.name: SSL Certificates
tags.description:
The **SSL** resource manages TLS certificates for HTTPS termination and mTLS authentication.

**Certificate Types**
- `server` — Server certificate for HTTPS termination (matched by SNI)
- `client` — Client certificate for mTLS with upstream services

APISIX dynamically selects the correct certificate based on the SNI (Server Name Indication) in the TLS handshake. Certificates can be rotated without restart.

To learn how to configure TLS certificates, see [SSL Certificates](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/certificate/).

tags.name: Secrets
tags.description:
The **Secret** resource integrates APISIX with external secret managers (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) for dynamic secret retrieval at runtime.

Once configured, you can reference a provider value through an APISIX Secret resource. For example, `$secret://vault/1/my-secret/key` uses the Vault Secret resource `1` to retrieve `key` from `my-secret`.

To learn how to configure secret managers, see [Secrets](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/terminology/secret/).

tags.name: Protos
tags.description:
The **Proto** resource stores Protocol Buffer (protobuf) `.proto` file content used by the `grpc-transcode` plugin to convert between HTTP/JSON and gRPC.

Upload your `.proto` definitions here, then reference them by ID in the `grpc-transcode` plugin configuration.

To learn how to configure gRPC transcoding, see [gRPC Transcode](https://apisix.apache.org/docs/apisix/next/plugins/grpc-transcode/).

tags.name: Schema Validation
tags.description: Endpoints for validating one resource or a complete declarative configuration without creating, persisting, or applying it.

tags.name: Standalone
tags.description: Endpoints exposed only when the deployment uses the YAML config provider (`deployment.role_data_plane.config_provider: yaml`).

protocol.description: Protocol scheme. Use `https` when `deployment.admin.https_admin` is enabled and `deployment.admin.admin_api_mtls.admin_ssl_cert` and `admin_ssl_cert_key` are configured.

host.description: Admin API host address. Configure via `deployment.admin.admin_listen` in `config.yaml`.

x-verification.limits: Static contract verification. Plugin Lua checks, certificate parsing, secret-reference bypasses, and live etcd/OpenResty behavior require integration testing.
